messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] elevated 5xx error rate detected for private-inference-gateway (us-west-2) — 5xx_rate=18% over last 5m. Affected: private endpoints for tenant ACME. Paging @Maya Chen (oncall-sre). :rotating_light:
Maya Chen: oncall here, looking. I see a cascade of 504/502 from gateway pools A and C. Metrics dashboard: latency + upstream connection resets. Starting triage — grabbing gateway logs and VPC NAT metrics.
Raj Patel: I'm pulling NAT metrics now. Quick note: NAT-A shows ephemeral port allocation at 97% (range 32768-61000). NAT-B is at 12%. Connections from private-inference-gateway cluster are heavily skewed to NAT-A.
Lina Gomez: Is there any recent route or healthcheck change for the transit appliances? Sticky mapping could keep sockets bound to the same NAT.
Maya Chen: Good call. Checking route-control logs... I see a route weight update at 2026-03-15T01:22:14Z that increased priority to NAT-A for the us-west transit set. Owner: deploy-bot (autopilot).
deploy-bot: automated rollout: adjusted route weights for us-west transit group -> {nat-a: 80, nat-b: 20} as part of canary config 2026-03-15. Triggered by latency test.
Priya Singh: Support seeing influx of tickets from ACME: "model request timed out" across multiple endpoints. Need customer message draft.
Tom Alvarez: ACME impact: interactive inference backends saw timeouts, throughput degraded. Estimated 6k requests failed over the last 10m, roughly 4% of their traffic. They're on dedicated private VPC.
Raj Patel: digging deeper — conntrack table on NAT-A is saturated, and ephemeral port churn high. I can see a pattern where long-lived model shard connections from our runtime reuse source ports and then create many short-lived child connections that consume ephemeral ports. Because the route weight shift concentrated traffic to NAT-A, its ephemeral space exhausted -> 5xx/timeout.
Lina Gomez: There's also an SG change log entry at 2026-03-15T00:58Z that tightened outbound ephemeral range on the transit appliance (rule id sg-0abcde). Could be contributing. Who changed that?
Maya Chen: That SG rule was applied by infra-config two hours ago as part of a security hardening; tag: harden-ephemeral. Rolling back would be last-resort. For immediate mitigation, we'll move traffic off NAT-A to NAT-B and scale transit pool.
Raj Patel: Preparing route flip now. Plan: set route weight nat-a: 10, nat-b: 90, then scale transit-appliances + reboot one NAT-A host to clear conntrack. Executing in 2 steps to avoid mass failover.
Maya Chen: :thumbsup: do the weight flip first, watch error rate + conntrack frees. If errors continue, drain NAT-A hosts. Notify customers after we see stabilization.
Raj Patel: (command) aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --route-table-id rtb-0x --association-id a-123 --set-weights '{"nat-a":10,"nat-b":90}'  // simulated
Raj Patel: route weights updated. Monitoring...
Lina Gomez: Observing connection rebalancing at the gateway. Upstream socket reuse continues but new flows now prefer NAT-B. Error rate trending down: 5xx dropped from 18% -> 6% in 3m.
Maya Chen: Good. Let's also scale transit pool by +2 instances (hot add) to increase NAT-B capacity while NAT-A drains. Raj, please also clear conntrack on the rebooted NAT-A host after draining.
Raj Patel: Scaling transit pool... scaling completed. Rebooting nat-a-03 to clear conntrack after draining.
Raj Patel: nat-a-03 drain complete, reboot done, conntrack tables cleared. Post-reboot ephemeral allocation for NAT-A now 11%.
Priya Singh: Drafted update for ACME and status page: short note about "Service degradation — transient NAT gateway translation saturation causing timeouts; mitigation in progress; no data exfiltration. Next update in 15m." Approving?
Tom Alvarez: Send now. I'd call customer engagement for ACME (priority outbound) and offer a zoom if they want live presence.
Maya Chen: Sent update. Monitoring full request success rate. Current top-level metrics: 5xx baseline ~0.7% pre-incident, peaked 18%, now down to 0.9% and flattening. Latency back to normal.
Lina Gomez: Root cause hypothesis: recent route weight change + tightened SG reduced effective translation capacity on NAT-A, creating heavy allocation skew and conntrack exhaustion. Combined with runtime behavior (socket reuse + many short-lived child flows) amplified exhaustion. We'll record RCA.
Maya Chen: Creating follow-up ticket ENG-1427: add alert for ephemeral allocation >85%, guardrails to prevent single NAT dominance, and revert autopilot route rollouts to stagger. Also action item: revert the SG hardening change or expand ephemeral range in prod.
Priya Singh: ACME acknowledged update and will watch. No escalations yet.
Maya Chen: Oncall handoff: I'm on shift for 30m, then handing to Raj. Raj will continue postmortem.
Raj Patel: Acknowledged. I'll follow up with NetOps postmortem and link to ENG-1427. Closing incident in 45m once we verify stability for 1 hour.
deploy-bot: rollout note: paused route-autopilot canary for us-west until ENG-1427 completes.
Maya Chen: summary: mitigation executed (route weight flip + scale + NAT reboot), error rate recovered to baseline. Root cause: allocation imbalance from route weight + SG change + runtime flow pattern. Next steps assigned. :white_check_mark:
